en: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, both from Jarir, from al-A'mash, from Habib, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: Usamah ibn Zayd and Sa'd were sitting talking together, and they both said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said... similar to their hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd ibn Malik, Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, and Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said... in the sense of the hadith of Shu'bah.

Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated it to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, except that he did not mention the story of Ata' ibn Yasar at the beginning of the hadith.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Habib, who said: We were in Medina when news reached me that the plague had broken out in Kufa. Ata' ibn Yasar and others said to me: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When you are in a land and it breaks out in it, do not depart from it; and when news reaches you that it is in a land, do not enter it." He said: I asked: "From whom?" They said: "From Amir ibn Sa'd who narrates it." He said: So I went to him, but they said: "He is away." He said: Then I met his brother, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, and asked him. He said: "I was present when Usamah was narrating to Sa'd, saying: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "This affliction is a punishment, or a torment, or a remnant of torment with which people before you were punished. So if it is in a land while you are in it, do not depart from it; and if news reaches you that it is in a land, do not enter it."'" Habib said: I said to Ibrahim: "Did you yourself hear Usamah narrating to Sa'd while he did not dispute it?" He said: "Yes."
Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated it to us: Abd al-Wahid—meaning Ibn Ziyad—narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, with the chain of transmission of Yunus, similar to his hadith.

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn Amr and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Amir ibn Sa'd informed me, from Usamah ibn Zayd, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "This affliction, or illness, is a punishment with which some nations before you were tormented; then it remained thereafter on earth, disappearing at one time and appearing at another. So whoever hears of it in a land should never proceed toward it, and whoever is in a land where it breaks out should never leave it fleeing from it."

Abu al-Rabi' Sulayman ibn Dawud and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us—they said: Hammad—and he is Ibn Zayd—narrated to us; (Second chain) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us; both of them from Amr ibn Dinar, with the chain of transmission of Ibn Jurayj, similar to his hadith.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Amr ibn Dinar informed me that Amir ibn Sa'd informed him that a man asked Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas about the plague. Usamah ibn Zayd said: "I will tell you about it: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'It is a punishment or a torment that Allah sent upon a group from the Children of Israel or people before you. So if you hear of it in a land, do not enter upon it; and if it enters upon you in a land, do not depart from it fleeing.'"

Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from Usamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, this plague is a torment that was visited upon those who came before you, or upon the Children of Israel. So if it is in a land, do not depart from it fleeing from it; and if it is in a land, do not enter it."

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us—they said: al-Mughirah informed us—and Ibn Qa'nab attributed him, saying: Ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Qurashi—from Abu al-Nadr, from Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The plague is a sign of punishment with which Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, tests people among His servants. So when you hear of it, do not enter upon it; and when it strikes a land while you are in it, do not flee from it." This is the hadith of al-Qa'nabi, and that of Qutaybah is similar to it.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I read to Malik, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir and Abu al-Nadr, the freed slave of Umar ibn Ubaydillah, from Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, that he heard him asking Usamah ibn Zayd: "What did you hear from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) concerning the plague?" Usamah said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The plague is a torment or a punishment sent upon the Children of Israel or upon those who were before you. So when you hear of it in a land, do not enter it; and when it strikes a land while you are in it, do not leave fleeing from it." And Abu al-Nadr said: "let nothing take you out except fleeing from it."

Amr ibn Zurarah narrated it to me: Abd al-Wahhab—meaning Ibn Ata'—informed us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that a man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "My brother's belly is disordered." He said to him: "Give him honey to drink," in the sense of the hadith of Shu'bah.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is that of Ibn al-Muthanna—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: A man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "My brother's bowels are loose." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Give him honey to drink." So he gave him honey to drink, then came back and said: "I gave him honey to drink, but it only increased his looseness." He said that to him three times, then came the fourth time, and he said: "Give him honey to drink." The man said: "I have given him honey to drink, but it only increased his looseness." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah has spoken the truth, and your brother's belly has lied." So he gave him honey to drink and he was cured.

Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather: Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, from A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that whenever someone died among her family and the women gathered for that and then dispersed except her immediate family and close relatives, she would order a pot of talbinah to be cooked, then tharid was prepared and the talbinah was poured over it. Then she would say: "Eat from it, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'Talbinah brings comfort to the heart of the sick and relieves some of the sorrow.'"

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us—they said: Isma'il—and he is Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no disease but that there is a cure for it in black seed, except death."

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah narrated it to me—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); (Second chain) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr al-Naqid, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us—they said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us; (Third chain) and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us; (Fourth chain) and Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us; all of them from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of the hadith of Uqayl. And in the hadith of Sufyan and Yunus: "the black seed," and he did not say "al-shuniz."

Muhammad ibn Rumh ibn al-Muhajir narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me that Abu Hurayrah informed them that he heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Indeed, in the black seed there is a cure for every disease except al-sam." And al-sam is death; and the black seed is al-shuniz.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me that Ibn Shihab informed him, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud informed me that Umm Qays bint Mihsan—and she was one of the early emigrant women who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and she was the sister of Ukkashah ibn Mihsan, one of the Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah—he said: She informed me that she came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with a son of hers who had not yet reached the age of eating solid food, and she had treated him by pressing his palate due to tonsillitis—Yunus said: "a'laqat" means she pressed his palate fearing he had tonsillitis—she said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Why do you torment your children with this throat-pressing? You should use this Indian incense wood"—meaning costus—"for indeed in it are seven cures, among which is for pleurisy." Ubaydullah said: And she informed me that that son of hers urinated in the lap of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called for water and sprinkled it over his urine, and did not wash it thoroughly.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sufyan: Musa ibn Abi A'ishah narrated to me, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah, from A'ishah, who said: We administered medicine by force into the corner of the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) during his illness, but he gestured: "Do not administer medicine to me." We said: "It is just the dislike of a sick person for medicine." When he regained consciousness, he said: "Let there remain none of you but that medicine is administered to him in the same way, except al-Abbas, for he was not present with you."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, Muhammad ibn Hatim, and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to us—they said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abayah ibn Rifa'ah: Rafi' ibn Khadij narrated to me, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Fever is from the boiling heat of Hell, so cool it down from yourselves with water." Abu Bakr did not mention "from yourselves," and said: He said: Rafi' ibn Khadij informed me.

Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Abayah ibn Rifa'ah, from his grandfather Rafi' ibn Khadij, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Indeed, fever is a boiling heat from Hell, so cool it down with water."

Abu Kurayb narrated it to us: Ibn Numayr and Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, with this chain of transmission. And in the hadith of Ibn Numayr: "she poured water between herself and the opening of her garment." And he did not mention in the hadith of Abu Usamah: "that it is from the heat of Hell." Abu Ahmad said: Ibrahim said: al-Hasan ibn Bishr narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, with this chain of transmission.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham, from Fatimah, from Asma': that a fever-stricken woman would be brought to her, so she would call for water and pour it into the opening of her garment, saying: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Cool it down with water," and he said: "It is from the heat of Hell."
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith and Abdah ibn Sulayman informed us, both from Hisham, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—they said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from A'ishah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Fever is from the heat of Hell, so cool it down with water."

Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn al-Hakam narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us; (Second chain) and Harun ibn Abdillah narrated to me—and the wording is his: Rawh narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd, from his father, from Ibn Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Fever is from the heat of Hell, so extinguish it with water."

Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Malik narrated to me; (Second chain) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us: al-Dahhak—meaning Ibn Uthman—informed us; both from Nafi', from Ibn Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Fever is from the heat of Hell, so extinguish it with water."

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father and Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us; (Second chain) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Numayr and Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us—they said: Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Indeed, severe fever is from the heat of Hell, so cool it down with water."

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us—they said: Yahya—and he is Ibn Sa'id—narrated to us, from Ubaydullah: Nafi' informed me, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Fever is from the heat of Hell, so cool it down with water."

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir; (Second chain) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Khaythamah informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was shot in his medial arm vein. He said: So the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) cauterized it with his own hand using a broad arrowhead; then it swelled, so he cauterized it a second time.
